title: Topline asks by traffic patterns — Sep 2026 synthesis
body:
Purpose:
This is a rapid synthesis of customer feedback collected between 2026-07 and 2026-08 (CS intake forms, account QBR notes, embedded support threads). Instead of clustering by persona or product area, we grouped asks by observed traffic patterns and operational pain points. The goal is to produce action-oriented requests that map to engineering experiments, console changes, and CS playbook updates.

Methodology (brief):
- Source signals: support tickets flagged as "performance/scale" or "billing surprise", QBRs for 12 strategic accounts, in-product feedback forms (n=87), and two customer interviews with infra/platform leads.
- Signal grouping: we labeled request context by traffic characteristic observed in logs: PEAK-BURST, LONG-TAIL (low qps but high token volume), STABLE-STEADY, and REGIONAL-REGULATORY spikes.
- Prioritization: impact (customer churn risk + revenue exposure) x implementation effort (rough bucket).

High-level summary (one-liner per cluster):
- PEAK-BURST: Customers need predictable, frictionless burst capacity and clearer costs when sudden traffic spikes occur (games, marketing blasts, ephemeral chatbots).
- LONG-TAIL: Startups and research teams on low QPS but heavy token workloads want smarter batching defaults and cost-attribution per feature.
- STABLE-STEADY: Mid-market SaaS customers demand SLA clarity per-route and per-model, plus deterministic latency for synchronous features.
- REGIONAL-REGULATORY: EU/UK customers require smoother Private/VPC onboarding, clearer data residency flags, and audit-ready logs tied to model versions.

Representative customer quotes (verbatim snippets from notes):
- "We went live with a promo and token costs spiked — we had no easy way to know which route or campaign did it." — major ecommerce platform
- "Our nightly embedding job runs for hours and we think quantization might help, but we can't test it without a dev clone of our Dedicated pool." — research startup
- "Latency jitter kills our UX. We need a strong SLA or an automatic fallback to a cheaper, faster model when the main one stalls." — fintech product manager

Grouped asks with proposed owner & rough priority:
1) Autoscale burst plan + predictable burst pricing (owner: product-dedicated; priority: high)
   - Ask: Allow configured burst pools + transparent per-minute charge estimate for bursts.
   - Why: Customers avoid promotions & campaigns because of unpredictable overage charges.
   - Quick idea: Add a "burst budget" toggle in Console > Dedicated; SMS/email alert when budget reaches 50%/80%.
   - Rough effort: 2–3 sprints (backend quota + billing UI)

2) Per-route token breakdown and campaign attribution (owner: console/observability; priority: high)
   - Ask: Token-level cost attribution by route/label + easy filter by date and API key.
   - Why: Billing surprise is the #1 churn trigger we logged.
   - Quick idea: Add per-request metadata ingestion (campaign_id header) + nightly rollups in Console billing tab.
   - Rough effort: 1–2 sprints

3) Dev-local Dedicated clone (sandbox harness) (owner: solutions-eng + infra; priority: medium-high)
   - Ask: Lightweight emulation of customer Dedicated config so teams can test quantization, batching, and warm cache effects before rolling to prod.
   - Why: Customers fear regressions; testing in staging is currently too divergent.
   - Quick idea: Dockerized runtime image + small GPU sandbox with knobbed limits; provide sample scripts to replay traces.
   - Rough effort: 2–4 sprints depending on scope

4) Default batching and KV-cache heuristics for long-tail workloads (owner: serving-runtime; priority: medium)
   - Ask: Smart defaults that detect low qps but long context and apply pre-configured batching/cache strategies to reduce per-token cost without degrading latency.
   - Why: Many small customers don't know how to tune batching; we can reduce costs and increase retention.
   - Quick idea: Telemetry-based suggested config in Optimize > Recommendations; 1-click apply.
   - Rough effort: 1–2 sprints (prototype)

5) Fast model-fallback routing policy (owner: routing/runtime; priority: medium)
   - Ask: Allow per-route fallback rules (e.g., fall back to gpt-mini/quantized variant after X ms or on queue depth threshold).
   - Why: Keeps user-facing features online during transient capacity issues.
   - Quick idea: Per-route JSON policy + metric-based trigger; expose simulations in Console.
   - Rough effort: 2–3 sprints

6) Streamlined Private/VPC onboarding checklist & audit bundle (owner: private-deployments + security; priority: high for EU/regulated accounts)
   - Ask: Packaged playbook, checklist, and pre-bundled audit logs for SOC/ISO reviews; sample network templates.
   - Why: Sales cycles stall on onboarding complexity and legal review friction.
   - Quick idea: "Private Starter Pack" doc + SOW template + sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippets.
   - Rough effort: docs + sample infra: 2–3 weeks; engineering: variable

Immediate quick wins (2–4 weeks):
- Billing alert templates for high token deltas by API key (CS can enable on behalf of customers).
- Console hint: "If you expect a burst > X tokens/min, consider enabling Burst Budget" (text + link).
- Small telemetry flag to capture campaign_id header for a subset of accounts for proof-of-concept.

Near-term experiments (1–3 months):
- Prototype per-route fallback with simulated traffic (target 3 accounts for pilot).
- Provide a lightweight sandbox image for Dedicated testing to 5 customers.
- Add Optimize suggestion flow for long-tail batching heuristics.

Strategic initiatives (quarter+):
- Integrated burst pricing product (billing + autoscale + SLA).
- Full private deployment onboarding automation (terraform modules + audit report generator).

Open questions / risks:
- Billing complexity: adding burst pricing may cannibalize committed revenue; requires finance input.
- Data retention & privacy for telemetry used in Optimize suggestions (legal review needed).
- Resource scheduling: sandbox Dedicated clones consume capacity — need a fair-usage policy.

Next steps / recommended owners:
- CS: roll out Billing Alert templates to top 30 at-risk accounts (owner: Jamal Okafor; ETA: 2 weeks).
- Product (Dedicated): scope Burst Budget ticket and get finance sign-off (owner: Priya Malhotra; ETA: start of next planning).
- Serving-runtime: triage long-tail batching POC with 2 engineers (owner: Daniel Kim; ETA: 1 sprint).
- Private: assemble Private Starter Pack docs and legal checklist (owner: Sofia Nguyen; ETA: 3 weeks).

Appendix (data snippets):
- 12 strategic accounts: 5 reported billing surprise incidents in last 90 days; 7 reported latency jitter affecting user flows.
- Sample support ticket IDs: CS-9821 (billing), CS-9874 (latency jitter), CS-9912 (private onboarding).

Notes to self / CS playbook snippets (for quick copy into shared checklist):
- "If a customer reports a sudden token spike, ask for: campaign_id, route name, time window, number of concurrent calls."
- "For customers on Dedicated considering quantization, offer sandbox replay and schedule an engineer pair session before production flip."

Bottom line: grouping asks by traffic behavior surfaced different levers than persona-only syntheses — many customers care less about model brand and more about predictability and clear remediation paths during spikes. Prioritize low-effort visibility features (billing alerts, campaign attribution) while scoping the longer product work (burst plans, private automation).

Document history: initial draft 2026-09-02 by Marisol; collab edits 2026-09-08; current in_review 2026-09-10.
